name: Behalf.bot — Voice Agent
description: Talk to the agent out loud. A local speech loop on the host: Whisper for hearing, Kokoro for speaking, and a small local model that answers what it can and escalates the rest to the full agent. Speech never leaves the machine; only escalated questions do. APPLE SILICON ONLY — the speech models are MLX, which does not run in the Linux container the rest of the chassis lives in.

platform.note: Not a container plugin. Whisper MLX and Kokoro MLX require Apple Silicon, and the process is managed by launchd on the host rather than by the chassis container. An install on Linux, Cloudflare or a managed host cannot run this.

requires.ollama: Local classifier and chat model. Must be reachable on the host.
requires.claude_cli: Escalations shell out to `claude -p` with the install's own .mcp.json, so the host needs Claude Code and a config. An install that does not run Claude Code locally cannot escalate.
requires.tailscale: Optional. run.sh publishes the browser client over the tailnet; drop that line to serve on localhost only.

enabled.description: Master toggle. False by default: this pulls several GB of models and only runs on Apple Silicon, so it is opt-in.

agent_name.description: What the operator calls the agent out loud. Used to detect being addressed by name, which is the strongest routing signal there is.

agent_name_variants.description: What speech recognition writes instead of the name. Not optional in practice: whisper-base renders 'Jax' as 'Jack' or 'Jacks' most of the time, and without these the agent does not know when it is being spoken to. Add whatever the logs show.

aliases_path.description: JSON map of what speech recognition writes to what the operator meant, applied once before anything reads the text. For names and shorthand a model would never guess - an internal tool called 'C1', a company acronym. See examples/aliases.example.json. Empty is fine.

sensitive_terms_path.description: JSON list of regexes that mark an utterance as too private to send anywhere. A match refuses the turn: nothing is escalated and the operator is told to handle it himself. It can only refuse, never route, which is what makes it safe to trust. NO DEFAULT TERMS SHIP - one person's private vocabulary is not another's. See examples/sensitive-terms.example.json.

answer_channel_id.description: Chat channel id where escalation answers get posted, so walking away mid-answer does not lose it. Spoken aloud as well when the room is quiet.

router_model.description: Ollama model that decides answer-locally versus escalate. Small and fast matters more than clever; this runs on every turn.

chat_model.description: Ollama model that answers the turns which never leave the box. A 3B is weak on anything substantive - raise it if small talk quality matters more than the extra latency.

stt_model.description: Whisper MLX repo. base is fast and adequate for English commands. For any language where a misheard word changes the meaning, use mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo: measured on European Portuguese, base heard 'com o prazo' where turbo heard 'como prazo', which is 'with the deadline' versus 'as the deadline'.

stt_language.description: ISO code passed to Whisper, or unset to auto-detect. Pin it when the operator speaks one language; leave it unset for a mixed-language conversation.

escalation_budget_usd.description: Per-question ceiling. A question that queries a database costs about $0.35, so a tight budget fails the turn rather than saving money.

escalation_timeout_secs.description: How long to wait for an escalated answer before giving up.

mcp_servers.description: Which MCP servers the escalation may boot, by name from the install's .mcp.json. Every server in that file starts before the model answers a word, so this list is a latency budget, not a capability wish list. Measured: no servers 4s, four servers 7s, fifteen servers never returned. Empty means no MCP at all, which is fastest and answers least.

sticky_session.description: Carry one escalation session across a conversation, so a follow-up knows what the previous turn was about. Also six times faster after the first question, because a resumed session stops re-paying for the system prompt and tool definitions.

port.description: Local port for the browser client.

serve_https_port.description: Tailscale serve port. Set 0 to skip publishing and stay on localhost.
